_what: The primary, nucleotide-resolved record of the TCF12::NR4A3 (TCF12/TEC) breakpoint in extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma, plus the two corroborating sources, committed here so no claim depends on the literature-cache branch.
_why: The junction-ASO coverage ladder's top row turned on whether the TCF12 exon assignment was reported or inferred. It said inferred, from a residue count. The authors of the primary report also DEPOSITED the chimeric cDNA, which resolves the junction to the nucleotide, and this repository had never retrieved it.
_what_this_is_not: Not a coverage measurement and not an efficacy claim.
Not a within-partner breakpoint DISTRIBUTION. It is ONE sequenced tumour; nothing here says how a second TCF12-rearranged tumour breaks.
Not a re-annotation of TCF12. The exon NUMBER is read against this repository's committed transcript model; the seam SEQUENCE is what the deposit itself carries.
_cost: $0 — three Europe PMC / NCBI E-utilities reads on a free GitHub Actions runner.
how_it_was_found: NCBI elink from the primary report's PubMed record to the nucleotide database (dbfrom=pubmed&db=nuccore&id=11156374) returned one direct submission, UID 13540159. An independent nuccore search for `TCF12 AND TEC AND chondrosarcoma` returned the same single UID. Neither route is a literature search, which is why 295 + 104 retrieved papers had not surfaced it: the breakpoint was never published as an exon in prose, it was DEPOSITED.

records.title: Fusion of the NH2-terminal domain of the basic helix-loop-helix protein TCF12 to TEC in extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma with translocation t(9;15)(q22;q21).
records.authors: Sjögren H, Wedell B, Meis-Kindblom JM, Kindblom LG, Stenman G.
records.abstract_verbatim: Extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcomas (EMCs) are characterized by recurrent t(9;22) or t(9;17) translocations resulting in fusions of the NH2-terminal transactivation domains of EWS or TAF2N to the entire TEC protein. We report here an EMC with a novel translocation t(9; 15)(q22;q21) and a third type of TEC-containing fusion gene. The chimeric transcript encodes a protein in which the first 108 amino acids of the NH2-terminus of the basic helix-loop-helix (bHLH) protein TCF12 is linked to the entire TEC protein. The translocation separates the NH2-terminal domain of TCF12 from the bHLH domain as well as from a potential leucine zipper domain located immediately downstream of the breakpoint. These results demonstrate that the NH2-terminal transactivation domains of EWS or TAF2N are not unique in their ability to convert the TEC protein into an oncogenically active fusion protein, and that they may be replaced by a domain from a bHLH protein that presumably endows the fusion protein with similar functions.
records.role: The report the deposit belongs to. Its ABSTRACT describes the chimera by residue count — 'the first 108 amino acids' — and names no exon, which is why this repository's assignment was an inference until the deposit was retrieved.

records.title: Genomic organization of human TCF12 gene and spliced mRNA variants producing isoforms of transcription factor HTF4.
records.authors: Gan TI, Rowen L, Nesbitt R, Roe BA, Wu H, Hu P, Yao Z, Kim UJ, O'Sickey T, Bina M.
records.abstract_verbatim: The human TCF12 gene, mapping to 15q21, encodes the helix-loop-helix transcription factor 4 (HTF4). A detailed analysis of this genomic region established the organization of the TCF12 gene. The gene includes 21 exons and is significantly larger than an average human gene. Preceding the second exon, two alternative acceptor sites for mRNA splicing yield two distinguishable transcripts (HTF4a and HTF4b) which differ in their 5' untranslated region but share identical coding sequences. Differential utilization of exon 15 in the TCF12 gene may reflect a mechanism producing a cell-type-specific protein (HTF4c). In addition, intron 5 in the TCF12 gene corresponds to the region involved in a translocation, t(9;15)(q22;q21), that results in a form of extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma.
records.role: An INDEPENDENT gene-structure paper, not a fusion paper. It states the TCF12 gene 'includes 21 exons' — the same count as this repository's committed transcript model, which is what makes its exon numbering comparable — and that 'intron 5 in the TCF12 gene corresponds to the region involved in a translocation, t(9;15)(q22;q21), that results in a form of extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma'. A genomic break in intron 5 splices exon 5 to the partner.

records.title: Molecular strategies for detecting chromosomal translocations in soft tissue tumors (review).
records.verbatim: Gene TCF12, also known as HTF4, presents different isoforms by alternative splicing and the breakpoint affects the region of intron 5 ( 158 , 159 ).
records.role: A review that states the intron-5 assignment in prose. ⚠ NOT an independent observation: its two citations at that sentence are the primary report and the gene-structure paper above, so it is a COMPOSITION of them, retrieved here to show that the exon assignment is not this repository's invention.

is_there_a_second_sequenced_TCF12_case.⭐_question: The 58-case partner cohort contains TWO TCF12 tumours and AF289510.1 is ONE sequenced chimera. A second deposit matching exon 5 would make the TCF12 arm a buildable RUNG instead of a bound priced at its ceiling — the difference between 95% being reachable for a junction-reagent panel and ~94.8% being the honest ceiling.
is_there_a_second_sequenced_TCF12_case.⛔_answer: NO. No second TCF12::NR4A3 sequence has been deposited, and the arm stays a bound. ⚠ THAT IS NOT A FINDING THAT THE JUNCTION IS PRIVATE — recurrence is UNTESTED, not refuted. Every later cohort that counted a TCF12 tumour counted it with an assay that cannot resolve an exon.

is_there_a_second_sequenced_TCF12_case.⭐_why_no_second_sequence_EXISTS_and_it_i: ⚠ CORRECTED 2026-08-15, AND THE CORRECTION MAKES THE EVIDENCE THINNER RATHER THAN THICKER. This sentence read 'COUNTED at least four times in independent cohorts'; the 2003 series is NOT an independent cohort — it re-reports the 2000 tumour, by its own citation. Read the count as: five reports name a TCF12 tumour, and after removing the index case's re-report, THREE independent cohorts (2014, 2021, 2023) count four tumours between them, none sequenced. TCF12-rearranged EMC has been COUNTED in independent cohorts and SEQUENCED once, in 2000. Every later count comes from a partner-level assay that cannot resolve an exon even in principle — the 26-case series called its TCF12 tumour by fluorescence in situ hybridization, and a break-apart or fusion FISH probe reports which genes are joined, never where. So the absence of a second junction is a property of how this disease is diagnosed, not evidence about how the second tumour breaks.

the_cohorts_that_count_a_TCF12_tumour.how_the_tcf12_case_was_resolved: cloned and SEQUENCED; deposited as AF289510.1
the_cohorts_that_count_a_TCF12_tumour.verbatim: The chimeric transcript encodes a protein in which the first 108 amino acids of the NH2-terminus of the basic helix-loop-helix (bHLH) protein TCF12 is linked to the entire TEC protein.
the_cohorts_that_count_a_TCF12_tumour.note: the only sequenced TCF12::NR4A3 junction in existence

the_cohorts_that_count_a_TCF12_tumour.how_the_tcf12_case_was_resolved: spectral karyotyping, FISH and RT-PCR — a fusion CALL, with no junction reported and no sequence deposited
the_cohorts_that_count_a_TCF12_tumour.verbatim: All tumors contained translocation-generated or cryptic gene fusions, including EWS-TEC (five cases, of which one was a novel fusion), TAF2N-TEC (four cases), and TCF12-TEC (one case).
the_cohorts_that_count_a_TCF12_tumour.⭐_SETTLED_2026_08_15_IT_IS_NOT_AN_INDEPE: ⚠ SUPERSEDED, RETAINED: 'SAME GROUP, SAME INSTITUTION as the 2000 report — Sjögren, Meis-Kindblom, Kindblom, Stenman, Göteborg — and it reports the same t(9;15)(q22;q21) in one case. It is LIKELY the SAME tumour re-reported in a series, and this file does NOT assert either way: the abstract does not say.' The abstract does not say. THE FULL TEXT DOES, and it says so in a citation rather than in prose: its Discussion reads 'We detected a fusion transcript in all 10 EMCs; EWS-TEC, TAF2N-TEC, and TCF12-TEC fusions were found in tumors from five, three, and one patient, respectively.' with references 12 and 15 attached to that sentence, and its reference 15 is 'Sjögren H, Wedell B, Meis-Kindblom JM, Kindblom L-G, Stenman G: Fusion of the NH2-terminal domain of the basic helix-loop-helix protein TCF12 to TEC in extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma with translocation t(9;15)(q22;q21). Cancer Res 2000' — PMID 11156374, the index report. Its Introduction says the same thing in the first person: 'We recently identified yet a third variant translocation t(9;15)(q22;q21) that generates a fusion of the NH2-terminal part of the basic helix-loop-helix transcription factor TCF12 to TEC.' with the same reference. And its Table 1 case 8 carries the karyotype '48,X,-Y,t(9;15)(q22;q21),+12,der(15)t(9;15)(q22;q21),+19[18]' — the index report's own translocation. ⛔ SO THE WORLD HOLDS ONE TCF12 TUMOUR WITH A JUNCTION CALL BEHIND IT, NOT TWO, and this cohort must not be counted as an independent observation of the partner.
the_cohorts_that_count_a_TCF12_tumour.⭐_provenance_of_the_three_quotes_above: Read from the PMC HTML of PMC1868116 fetched at HTTP 200 from https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1868116/ (the fetch header is preserved in the retrieved file). ⚠ THE EARLIER ATTEMPT LOOKED FOR THE WRONG THING: `⚠_the_two_full_texts_that_would_settle_the_double_counting` records fullTextXML returning HTTP 404 and concluded the abstracts were the record. Europe PMC's fullTextXML endpoint 404s for a paper PMC serves perfectly well as HTML — an absent reading of one endpoint was read as absence of the text (CLAUDE.md §4).
the_cohorts_that_count_a_TCF12_tumour.⚠_a_second_defect_in_this_series_found_i: ITS PARTNER COUNTS ARE TUMOUR-LEVEL, NOT PATIENT-LEVEL, AND THE TWO DIFFER. The abstract says 'TAF2N-TEC (four cases)'; the Discussion says three patients. Table 1's own footnote reconciles them: 'Case 6 I and II represent two separate metastases from one patient.' (A second footnote, 'Case 4 A, B, and C represent different parts of the same tumor', collapses three rows to one tumour on the other arm.) So this series is 5 EWSR1 / 3 TAF15 / 1 TCF12 over NINE patients, not ten, and pooling its abstract's integers into a partner prevalence would double-count a patient — POLICY-evidence.md §2.3's within-study rule, which requires mutually exclusive strata. Recorded here because this series is otherwise an attractive addition to a partner denominator: it is fully accounted, every case fusion-positive, and karyotyped.

is_there_a_second_sequenced_TCF12_case.⛔_what_this_licenses_and_what_it_does_no: LICENSES: keeping the TCF12 row a BOUND, and saying WHY in a way that survives review — the junction is resolved, the reagent exists and is screened, and the within-partner distribution rests on one tumour. DOES NOT LICENSE: calling the junction private, rare, or non-recurrent. Four cohorts counted a TCF12 tumour and none of them looked at the junction, so the recurrence question has never been ASKED, let alone answered.

⚠_the_two_full_texts_that_would_settle_t._what: Whether PMID 12598313's TCF12 case IS the 2000 tumour is the one question this search leaves open, and it decides whether the world holds two TCF12 tumours with a junction call or one.
⚠_the_two_full_texts_that_would_settle_t.reading: ⚠ SUPERSEDED FOR PMC1868116, RETAINED: 'Both carry a PMCID and neither is in Europe PMC's open-access full-text subset, so the abstracts are the record.' The second clause was an inference from ONE endpoint's 404 and it was wrong for the paper that mattered — PMC serves PMC1868116's full text as HTML at HTTP 200. The half that was right and stays right: neither paper reports a junction, so neither can supply a second exon-resolved breakpoint whatever its full text says. The open question was a COUNT, not a junction.
⚠_the_two_full_texts_that_would_settle_t.⭐_CLOSED_2026_08_15_FOR_THE_ONE_THAT_DEC: PMID 12598313's TCF12 case IS the 2000 tumour, established from its own citations and its own Table 1 karyotype — see `the_cohorts_that_count_a_TCF12_tumour[1]`. PMC4015728 (PMID 24746215, MSKCC 2014) is a different institution on another continent and was never the doubtful one.
⚠_the_two_full_texts_that_would_settle_t.cost_to_close: ⚠ SUPERSEDED, RETAINED: 'a publisher fetch or an interlibrary request — not a $0 route'. It was a $0 route and had been all along: the same PMC article the fullTextXML call 404ed on serves its full text as HTML. Cost to close, actually incurred: one HTTP GET. ⛔ THE LESSON IS THE ONE CLAUDE.md §4 STATES — an open question priced as expensive stops being re-examined, and this one sat as the single named unknown in a file whose whole subject is how many TCF12 tumours exist.
